newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely up, Dec hits contract low.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely up, Dec hits contract low.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed barely firmer after the benchmark December contract slipped to a new life-of-contract low for the fourth time in a week.
Continued speculative selling pressured December under its previous contract low of 73.30 cents to 73.20 cents, where trade buying stymied further losses.
"The trade was an aggressive buyer, particularly at the end of day to bring us over unchanged," a floor source said.
Analysts said Tuesday's spec/hedge report could determine whether the market will stabilize or continue to erode.
"If the report shows the specs are only 10 percent net short it could be a little bearish," the dealer said, adding that expectations for a 20 percent net short position are already in the market.
Support in December remained at 72.00 cents followed by 70.35 cents, the now-expired July contract low.
Some analysts said the market is oversold and should begin to retrace losses in next several days. Resistance in December was pegged at 74.10 cents followed by 74.50 and 75.00 cents.
The December contract ended 0.12 cent higher at 73.47 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.70 to 73.20 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.15 higher to 0.10 cent lower.
An estimated 7,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Friday's official 12,739 lots.
